items.title: Wildfires, heatwaves threaten global air quality and health, UN warns
items.summary: Wildfires and heatwaves are threatening global efforts to improve air quality and protect human health, the World Meteorological Organisation said on Monday. The UN agency warned that increasingly severe fires are raising exposure to toxic PM2.5 pollution, even as regulations have reduced industrial and transport emissions in Europe and North America.

items.title: Market Operations by the Bank of Japan (Aug.)
US envoys bring ‘more effective’ Ukraine peace proposals to Kyiv, official says
items.summary: US envoys brought new, “more effective” proposals to Kyiv aimed at ending the war with Russia, a senior Ukrainian presidential official said on Sunday. President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner described talks positively but announced no breakthrough, as Zelensky warned fighting could continue into winter.

items.title: "Ready to talk": German far-right celebrates victory
items.summary: “Everything is possible” is the election campaign slogan of the far-right Alternative for Germany, the leader in Saxony-Anhalt, where the polls have just closed. It talks of a seminal moment for the country. Ulrich Siegmund, who has been polling in pole position to become the state leader, knows he has history in his grasp.

items.title: AfD could lead "the first far-right state government since the dark days of Nazism"
items.summary: Voting is underway in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election. "If the AfD does form a government in Saxony-Anhalt, that would make it the first regional government headed by a far-right party since the end of the Second World War, since the dark days of Nazism", our correspondent Nick Holdsworth explains.

items.title: A Bright Spot at Mount Michael
items.summary: With austral winter nearing its end, clouds cleared for a satellite view of volcanic activity in the remote South Atlantic.

items.title: ‘Advance safety for all’: International police cooperation helps tackle cross-border crime
items.summary: As criminal networks increasingly exploit weak institutions and operate across borders, the UN says no police force can tackle them alone.

items.title: Germany: What could change in Saxony-Anhalt if the AfD wins?
items.summary: Voting began in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election. Recent surveys place the AfD at just over 40%, followed by Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU) at 23%. If the AfD wins, "one of the main things they want to change is the education system. They say they want to reset education," our journalist Shirli Stibon explains.

items.title: Under-fire FIFA boss Infantino to seek re-election despite calls to resign
items.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino plans to seek his fourth and final term in next year’s election, despite the outrage sparked by his now-shelved plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. “Nothing has changed,” a spokesman for football’s governing body confirmed on Sunday, referring to an announcement Infantino made back in April.

items.title: The week in pictures: Nepal rescue operations, World Nomad Games and Russian strikes on Kyiv
items.summary: From the desperate search for workers trapped in the hydropower tunnels buried by the catastrophic flooding in Nepal to crowds of women mourning the victims of a US bombardment of a wedding in southern Iran, FRANCE 24 looks back at the week's most striking pictures.

items.title: Germany: Why is the AfD so popular in Saxony-Anhalt?
items.summary: Voting began in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election that could see the Alternative for Germany (AfD) become the first far-right party to lead a state government since World War II. We discuss this with our guest, Hans Stark, professor of German studies at Sorbonne University.

items.title: German exit polls suggest far-right party has big lead in regional election
items.summary: Exit polls show Germany's AfD taking a commanding lead in a regional election, but it remains unclear whether the far-right party can form the country's first state government since World War II.

items.title: Monetary Base and the Bank of Japan's Transactions (Aug.)
Bank of Japan's Transactions with the Government (Aug.)
Germany's far-right AfD clear frontrunner in eastern state vote
items.summary: German voters headed to the polls on Sunday for a key regional election in the ex-communist east where the far-right, anti-immigrant, Moscow- and Trump-friendly AfD is expected to secure an easy majority. Our correspondent Nick Holdsworth tells us more.

items.title: Ethan Hawke receives the Deauville Talent Award
items.summary: Known for starring in Dead Poets Society, the Before trilogy and Boyhood, Hollywood legend Ethan Hawke receives the #Deauville #Talent #Award in recognition of his career spanning nearly 40 years. He also plays the lead role in The Weight, screened at the Opening Ceremony of the 52nd Deauville #American #Film #Festival and due to be released in theaters on September 16. Our reporter Gaëlle Fonseca spoke to him on the red carpet.

items.title: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll quits: "What we've seen is almost a factional clash"
items.summary: Amid the US conflict with Iran, Democrats and some Republicans are warning of a leadership void at the top of the US military. That's after the resignation this week of the Army's top civilian official, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, amid widespread reports of tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Our guest, Walter Ladwig, associate professor of international relations at King's College London, tells us more.

items.title: Middle East Live: Israel army orders evacuation of zone in south Lebanon ahead of strikes
items.summary: The Israeli army demanded early Monday that residents of Deir Zahrani in southern Lebanon leave a specific zone ahead of strikes against Iran-backed Hezbollah. Hezbollah's Al-Manar television channel later reported Israeli airstrikes on Deir Zahrani. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

items.title: EU to boost Greenland investment amid Trump annexation claims
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is expected to announce increased EU investment in Greenland on Monday, including in critical minerals, satellite communications and renewable energy. Her two-day visit signals support for Greenland and Denmark amid US President Donald Trump’s push for American control of the Arctic territory.

items.summary: "We achieved within a few years what had taken the European space industry decades before."
